The prose plan cannot answer 'is this wave done?' — this file can, via scripts/wave-status.sh.
Items with no `issue` are recorded as 'informal': work done directly off the plan with no
issues/NNN-*.md behind it. That is exactly the gap that made false completion claims cheap,

Not backfilling issue files retroactively for already-shipped Wave 0 items: they are landed and
verified, and inventing DoDs after the fact would be documentation theatre. New work gets a real
issue file first — see docs/agents/staff-engineer-agent.md Mode E.

2026-07-29: #307 approach DECIDED (owner: manual is a hard no). Automated discovery via robots.txt Sitemap: harvesting + narrowing to page-type child sitemaps. Evidence: a blind /events guess costs the shop a 249,540-byte styled Shopify 404; the sitemap index is 10,334 bytes and separates sitemap_pages from sitemap_products/collections/blogs. So automation is ~25x LIGHTER on the store than the manual guess — no efficiency-vs-respect trade-off. PART 1 LANDED: RobotsPolicy retains Sitemap: (document-level per RFC 9309 2.2.4, de-duplicated), surfaced through fetch_path -> /fetch -> ScraperClient at zero marginal request cost; 7 Rust tests + mutation-probed. REMAINING: (a) generic /sitemap-urls endpoint in the scraper with a HARD per-store request+byte budget enforced where the requests happen (politeness as an invariant, not an intention); (b) Stacks.Enrichment.EventsPath.resolve/1 deep module applying the domain filter (events|whats-on|calendar|diary|programme) and persisting events_path or unscrapable_reason so we never ask twice; (c) wire the job off @events_path; (d) conditional requests (ETag/If-Modified-Since) — entirely absent today, and the single biggest politeness win.

2026-07-29: ⛔ PLAN SHAPE CHANGED — #307 is now BLOCKED on new issue #308. Trying to read both shops' sitemap indexes (to ground the child-selection policy in fact rather than guesswork) returned HTTP 429 + a 9KB bot-challenge page on EVERY path of BOTH domains, /robots.txt included, after only a handful of requests from one laptop. Live probing of these two domains stopped there. Two defects behind it, one root cause — the service had no channel for a shop to say 'slow down': (a) `retry_after_seconds` was configured for both shops and read by NO code; a 429 was recorded as a FAILURE, melting the fuse shared by every store, on every attempt while paced. (b) worse: `classify_status` mapped 400..=499 to NoRestrictions, so a 429 on /robots.txt granted UNRESTRICTED crawl permission — and cached it in the domain's OnceCell for the process lifetime. Both fixed under #308 with 4 mutation probes. Harvesting politely through a client that ignores an explicit 'stop' would have been theatre, so #308 goes first.
